title: Resolution, aspect ratio and the pixel budget

questions.q: You type a width of 1333 and a height of 750 into Empty Latent Image. What size does the decoded picture have?
questions.why: The latent is made with height // 8 and width // 8, which is 93 by 166, and the VAE decodes that to 8 times as much. The lab prints 1328x744 and 11,718 pixels lost.

questions.q: A picture has aspect ratio r = W / H and the budget is P pixels. What is the width before rounding?
questions.why: W × H = P and W / H = r give W² = P × r. The height is √(P / r). The Scale Image to Total Pixels node applies the same square root through its scale factor.

questions.q: Scale Image to Total Pixels with a budget of 1 megapixel and resolution_steps 64 turns a 3000 by 2000 image into 1280 by 832. What is notable about that result?
options: It is exactly on the budget
It is 1.0156 times the budget, because rounding to the nearest multiple of 64 can overshoot
It is below the budget by 1.56%
Its sides are not multiples of 64
questions.answer: It is 1.0156 times the budget, because rounding to the nearest multiple of 64 can overshoot
questions.why: The node rounds each side to the nearest multiple, not down. The lab row for 3000x2000 at step 64 shows 1.0156 and a ratio error of +0.0256, and 1280x832 is not on SDXL's list of 40 sizes.

questions.q: Doubling both sides of a square image multiplies its pixel count by 4. By how much does the N × N attention matrix grow if every latent position attends to every other?
questions.why: N = (side / 8)², so doubling the side multiplies N by 4 and N × N by 16. The lab shows 16,777,216 entries at 512 and 268,435,456 at 1024.

questions.q: What does FlashAttention change about self-attention?
options: It computes the same exact attention with memory that grows linearly with sequence length, while the number of comparisons still grows as N squared
It approximates attention so that the N squared comparisons disappear
It removes the need for a GPU
It shrinks the latent before attention
questions.answer: It computes the same exact attention with memory that grows linearly with sequence length, while the number of comparisons still grows as N squared
questions.why: The FlashAttention paper describes an IO-aware exact algorithm and reports a memory footprint that grows linearly with sequence length, with runtime that still grows quadratically.

questions.q: A 1920 by 1080 image goes through Scale Image to Total Pixels with megapixels 1.0 and resolution_steps 64. What comes out?
options: 1344 by 768, one of the 40 sizes SDXL was fine-tuned on
questions.answer: 1344 by 768, one of the 40 sizes SDXL was fine-tuned on
questions.why: The scale factor is √(1048576 / 2073600), about 0.711, which gives 1365.3 by 768 before rounding. Rounding to multiples of 64 gives 1344 by 768, whose height 768 and width 1344 appear in the paper's Appendix I.
